If the patient does not respond to painful stimuli, do not move them as you could cause further injury. 3. Check for signs of pulse, respiration, and defecation. 4. Do not pull it out directly as you can cause further injury to the patient. 9. Place a clean cloth or gauze over the wound to wipe away any dirt or debris. 10. Cover the wound with a sterile dressing and apply pressure to stop the bleeding. If the bleeding is not stopped within 10 minutes, apply firm manual pressure to the wound with clean gloved hands or cloth. If the bleeding continues, call emergency medical services again and inform them of the situation. 11. If possible, elevate the bleeding limb above the heart to slow down the bleeding. 12. If available, apply a tourniquet to the affected limb, but only after you have controlled the bleeding at the wound site. Make sure to release the tourniquet every 20 to 30 minutes to avoid further injury to the patient.
